Decide whether this exchange contains a motte-and-bailey move.

Structure: a speaker makes Claim A. A different person challenges it (Challenge C). The ORIGINAL speaker replies with Claim B.

Label MOTTE_BAILEY if Claim B retreats to a narrower, weaker or more easily defensible position than Claim A, while presenting that retreat as if it still defends Claim A (treating the weaker claim as equivalent to the original one).
Label NONE if Claim B is an honest clarification, adds detail, restates the same position, or openly concedes the point. Ordinary disagreement or clarification is NONE.

Claim A: [Content note: reference to the Holocaust, a standard meta-ethics example] You have no more objective standing to call Hitler evil than he'd have calling you evil -- morality appears to be a non-empirical, human-created concept.

Challenge C: That's extreme, indefensible moral relativism -- I reject any moral framework that doesn't let me call Hitler evil.

Claim B: It's not relativism, it's closer to moral existentialism -- there's no inherent morality, but we still need one to function, so we choose one. I'm not saying you CAN'T call Hitler evil, I'm just saying you can't PROVE it's objectively true.

Respond with exactly this JSON: {"label": "MOTTE_BAILEY" or "NONE", "reason": "<one sentence>"}
